whoWeAre.bannerSub: Your local pharmacy® — independently owned, community driven.
whoWeAre.introPara1: Guardian, I.D.A., and Remedy'sRx pharmacies are independently owned and operated by local pharmacists who dedicate their practice to the best possible patient care — beyond just prescriptions.
whoWeAre.introPara2: With over 1,400 locations coast to coast, both in urban and rural areas, our independent pharmacies reflect the values of the communities they serve. Each pharmacy is unique, but they are all united in the pledge to uphold what being an independent pharmacy stands for — empowering patients to live a healthy life by providing unrivaled, compassionate, holistic health care.

boxes.title: Returning your Medications Safely
boxes.text1: When was the last time you cleaned out your medicine cabinet? If you look hard enough, you may find expired or unused medications. These could include tablets purchased for prevention of illness during travel, unused pain medications, leftover cough syrup, or outdated birth control pills.
boxes.text2: Do not flush, pour down the sink or throw any of your medications in the garbage. Taking any of these actions can put you, your community and the environment at risk. Instead, visit your nearest pharmacy and let us dispose of them safely on your behalf.

boxes.title: Injections and Needles
boxes.text1: If your medication requires self-injection, your pharmacist can show you the right technique.
boxes.text2: You can also bring back sharp bins at your pharmacy for safe disposal.

cards.title: Step 1
cards.text1: Gather any unwanted or expired prescription medication, over-the-counter medication or natural health products.

cards.title: Step 2
cards.text1: Remove any personal or identifying information from the medication, if applicable. Do not mix medical sharps and medication.

cards.title: Step 3
cards.text1: Find your nearest pharmacy and drop by at your earliest convenience.

vaccinations.introPara1: Vaccination is one of the most effective ways to protect yourself and your family against common diseases. Our pharmacists offer a wide range of vaccination services for children and adults.
vaccinations.introPara2: Whether you're updating your vaccine booklet or preparing for flu season, your MarkhaMack pharmacist is there to help guide you and administer the vaccines so you can focus on what matters most.

vaccinations.vaccinesIntro: Vaccine availability and funding varies by province and location*. These are the vaccines available in Ontario:
vaccinations.familyIntro: Learn more about vaccines that help shield you against common diseases:

familyCards.title: Flu, COVID-19 & Other Respiratory Viruses
familyCards.text: Vaccination can protect you against different respiratory viruses (flu, COVID-19, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and pneumococcus). Some vaccines are recommended every year, others only after a certain age.

familyCards.title: Travel Vaccines
familyCards.text: Depending on your destination, some immunizations should be considered before and after your trip for maximum safety. Make sure to book an appointment at least 6 weeks in advance to ensure you are fully immunized.

familyCards.title: Other Diseases
familyCards.text: Vaccination can minimize your risk of contracting several diseases, such as shingles, tetanus, hepatitis and certain childhood illnesses.

cards.title: Flu
cards.text1: Highly contagious infection of the respiratory tract caused by the influenza virus. Recommended every year.
cards.text2: Recommended for: Everyone 6 months and older.

cards.title: COVID-19
cards.text1: Infection caused by the constantly evolving SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus. Recommended every year.
cards.text2: Recommended for: People aged 70 and over, or with a weakened immune system or chronic illness.

cards.title: Tetanus
cards.text1: Caused by the bacterium Clostridium tetani, which can enter the body through a cut or bite wound.
cards.text2: Recommended for: Everyone. *Availability varies by province

cards.title: Hepatitis A & B
cards.text1: Contagious liver infections caused by a virus. The chances of contracting the virus increase when traveling to certain parts of the world.

cards.title: HPV
cards.text1: Human papillomavirus (HPV) is a sexually-transmitted virus.
cards.text2: Recommended for: Everyone, as of 3rd grade.

cards.title: Measles
cards.text1: A serious and highly contagious disease, spread through the air when an infected person breathes, coughs, sneezes or speaks.
cards.text2: Recommended for: Children aged 12 to 18 months and all those who have never been vaccinated. *Availability varies by province

cards.title: Whooping Cough
cards.text1: Also known as pertussis, a highly contagious disease that causes severe, uncontrollable coughing fits.
cards.text2: Recommended for: Infants aged 2 months and over, and pregnant women. *Availability varies by province

cards.title: Pneumococcal Infections
cards.text1: Infections caused by the Streptococcus pneumonia bacteria.
cards.text2: Recommended for: People with a chronic illness or over 65.

cards.title: Shingles
cards.text1: Shingles happen when the virus that causes chickenpox stays in your body and can reactivate at any time during your life.
cards.text2: Recommended for: Ages 18+ for those at increased risk, and ages 50+.

cards.title: RSV
cards.text1: The respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a seasonal virus that circulates from fall to spring.
cards.text2: Recommended for: People aged 60 and over.

sections.heading: Vaccines against respiratory viruses
sections.intro: The following vaccines against respiratory viruses are available to the public. Ask your pharmacist if these vaccines are offered in store.

cards.text1: The flu is much more serious than the common cold and can lead to health complications.
The flu virus changes every year and so does the vaccine. For the best protection, you should get vaccinated every year.
Not everyone is well equipped to overcome the flu. Avoid spreading the flu to your loved ones with a flu shot.
It's easy! Just visit your local pharmacy.

boxes.title: The flu is a serious infection
boxes.text1: The flu is a highly contagious infection that causes symptoms such as fever, cough, muscle aches and severe fatigue. For a healthy person, the flu will cause a lot of discomfort but will usually resolve without complications. For people with health issues, however, the flu can lead to hospitalization or even death. For these people, getting vaccinated every year is a good way to protect themselves against the flu.

boxes.title: Who is most at risk?
boxes.text1: Everyone can get the flu, including healthy adults. In fact, every year, 5-20% of adults will catch the virus. However, some people are at higher risk of flu related complications:
list: People over 65 years old and children under 5 years old
Pregnant women and those planning to become pregnant
Residents of long-time care facilities
People with chronic diseases such as diabetes

travel_vaccines.introPara1: If you are planning to travel, it is important to check vaccination recommendations or requirements, as these vary from country to country.
travel_vaccines.introPara2: Pharmacists who offer travel vaccination services can prescribe or administer the required vaccines.
travel_vaccines.introPara3: They can also check that you are up to date with your basic vaccinations and prescribe a booster shot when necessary.
travel_vaccines.introPara4: Consult your pharmacist at least 6 weeks before your departure date to make sure you have the necessary vaccinations and advice.

diabetes.introHeading: To keep an eye on your diabetes
diabetes.introPara1: Whether you have prediabetes, diabetes or are newly diagnosed, many tests exist to ensure your blood sugar is well under control and that your treatment is working well.

cards.title: A1C Test
cards.text1: For pre-diabetics and diabetics, A1C is an important test that indicates if your diabetes is well managed, over a short period of time. This finger prick blood test takes 5 minutes and can be done at any time. Taking this test will help you adjust your treatment to avoid diabetes-related complications.

cards.title: Blood Sugar Readings
cards.text1: You can get your blood sugar readings at your pharmacy. It only requires a quick needle prick on your fingertip. You can then discuss your results with your pharmacist and learn about the best practices to get accurate readings.

cards.title: Self-Monitoring Education
cards.text1: Monitoring your blood glucose is an important part of managing your diabetes. If you wish to use a blood glucose monitor at home, your pharmacist can suggest the best one for your needs and explain how you can use it.

cards.title: Hypertension Monitoring
cards.text1: You can get your blood pressure readings done in participating pharmacies using their on-site devices. These results can then be added to your personal health record. With this data, your pharmacist can ensure your medication is doing what it should and that your blood pressure is within normal ranges.

cards.title: Self-Monitoring Education
cards.text1: If you'd rather take your blood pressure in the comfort of your home, you can rely on blood pressure monitors. Your pharmacist can suggest the best practices to get accurate readings and recommend devices that will meet your needs.

cards.title: Anticoagulant Treatment Monitoring (INR)
cards.text1: If you are taking warfarin or anticoagulants, blood tests are necessary to ensure that your anti-clotting medication is on target. Your pharmacist can prescribe this test as needed and adjust your medication. You do not need to have a heart condition to get this test.

cards.title: Cholesterol Monitoring
cards.text1: Getting your cholesterol levels checked is an important step of preventing heart-related diseases and stroke, especially since there are usually no symptoms associated with high cholesterol. Your pharmacist can prescribe this simple blood test if needed and make sure your cholesterol medication is working as it should.

infoBoxes.heading: Substituting a brand-name drug with a generic drug
infoBoxes.text: Don't hesitate to ask your pharmacist if a generic version of a prescribed drug exists. A generic drug is pharmaceutically equivalent to a brand-name drug: it contains the same active medicinal ingredients, in the same quantities, in a comparable dosage form.

blocks.text: There are many good reasons to use compression socks, whether you have poor blood circulation, want to soothe heavy and tired legs or are planning to take a long flight. Your pharmacist will help you choose the right model, size and material for the best fit possible.

maternity_pregnancy.introPara1: Looking to get pregnant? Your pharmacist can accompany you through the whole process until the baby arrives.

cards.title: Advice on Vitamins
cards.text1: Folic acid plays an essential role in the development of your baby, even before the very first weeks of life. Ideally, you should start taking a supplement at least three months before stopping contraception. Talk to your pharmacist before choosing a product.

cards.title: Advice on Medication
cards.text1: Some medication should be avoided during pregnancy or if you are breastfeeding because they can be harmful to the baby. Before taking any medication, talk to your pharmacist to know more about potential adverse effects. If your little one is in need of OTC medication, your pharmacist can offer advice on the best way to administer it.

cards.title: Pregnancy-Related Symptoms
cards.text1: Nausea and acid reflux are common side effects pregnant women may experience. While they're usually not serious, they can be pretty unpleasant. Your pharmacist can help you manage your symptoms while ensuring there are no risks for the baby.

cards.title: Gestational Diabetes
cards.text1: If you develop gestational diabetes during the course of your pregnancy and must take insulin to control it, your pharmacist will show you how and give you tips on how to manage your condition, including advice on how to monitor your blood glucose at home.

cards.title: Breastfeeding
cards.text1: If you are a new mother, you may need a breast pump. Fortunately, it is possible to rent this device and all its accessories in participating pharmacies. Your pharmacist can also explain how to use it and how to clean your breast pump equipment.

cards.title: App and Home Deliveries
cards.text1: Let your pharmacist come to you: use our app to get your prescriptions prepared ahead of time or to set up home delivery services. This might be useful towards the end of your pregnancy or when your baby is home with you.

boxes.text1: Never underestimate the effect of food on your treatment. When your pharmacist gives you specific instructions regarding food, be sure to follow them! Otherwise, your treatment may not be fully effective or may even lead to side effects that could have been avoided.

boxes.title: 5 FOOD CATEGORIES THAT INTERACT WITH YOUR MEDICATION
boxes.text1: Discover why it’s important not to pair your medication with certain foods like grapefruit, dairy products or even caffeine, and what happens if you do.

cards.title: Medication: with or without food?
cards.text1: Discover how foods can have an impact on efficacy and effects of your medication, and why some medication must be taken on an empty stomach while others not.

cards.title: The benefits of water
cards.text1: Discover why water should be your drink of choice to quench your thirst, and how much you should drink per day.

cards.title: How to treat and prevent diseases with diet
cards.text1: A balanced diet is essential to staying healthy. It's also an integral part of your treatment and can act as a preventive measure for numerous diseases.

cards.title: 5 foods that interact with medication
cards.text1: Discover why it’s important to be careful about consuming certain foods like grapefruit, dairy products, and foods rich in potassium if you take medication.

cards.title: PRESCRIPTIONS
cards.text1: Your pharmacist can prescribe medication for a minor health problem right away, provide advice on products or help you manage the medication you take for a chronic condition.

cards.title: WEIGHT MANAGEMENT
cards.text1: If you’re thinking about losing weight, your pharmacist can shed a light on helpful products and make sure your medication doesn’t make you gain weight as a side effect.

cards.title: MEDICATION CUSTOMIZATION
cards.text1: Sticking to your medication isn’t always a walk in the park. Your pharmacist is here to make minor or major adjustments to your therapy or provide you with custom formulas and innovative packaging to make it all easier.

mental_health.introPara1: 1 in 3 Canadians will experience a mental health problem in their lifetime. Mental health disorders are challenging for people living with them as well as their loved ones, but these conditions can be overcome with appropriate treatment and help of your pharmacist.

boxes.title: PHARMACIST TIPS
boxes.text1: Managing mental health conditions is challenging. It’s already hard enough to remember to take your medication on a regular basis on top of everything else. Let your pharmacist help you manage prescription renewals by synchronizing refill dates.
boxes.text2: Your pharmacist can also assist you in your role as caregiver, and can refer you to support networks, as needed.

boxes.title: ANXIETY OR PANIC ATTACK?
boxes.text1: We all, at some point in our lives, experience certain events that upset us to varying degrees and trigger a lot of anxiety. Sometimes you may feel so overwhelmed by your emotions that you lose control and experience a panic attack.

cards.title: Discontinuing Antidepressants
cards.text1: Stopping your antidepressant treatment too soon increases the risk of relapse. Learn when and how to come off antidepressants.

cards.title: Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (ADHD)
cards.text1: Learn about attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) and the symptoms of this neurological disorder.

cards.title: Work-Family Balance
cards.text1: Juggling work, family life, and other obligations can be stressful and exhausting. Discover a few ways to help you balance work and family.

cards.title: Insomnia
cards.text1: Certain pre-bedtime activities and habits can have a negative impact on your sleep. Learn all about good sleep hygiene to help prevent insomnia and difficulty sleeping.

cards.title: MENTAL HEALTH SUPPORT
cards.text1: Your pharmacist offers private consultations to discuss your personal situation, assess your current medication, talk about alternative options and make sure your side effects are not disruptive.

cards.title: MEDICATION ADJUSTMENT
cards.text1: With some adjustments from your pharmacist, side effects can be minimized, harmful drug interactions can be limited and dosages can be decreased in a way that is not detrimental to your well-being.

cards.title: MEDICATION LIST
cards.text1: Having a list of your medication on hand in case of emergency, travel or a doctor appointment can be quite useful. Ask your pharmacist to prepare it.

skin_health.introPara1: There are a lot of different skin conditions and it may be difficult to recognize or to treat them efficiently.
skin_health.introPara2: When in doubt, don’t hesitate to ask your pharmacist, he or she can give you advice on your individual needs.

boxes.title: SERVICES FROM YOUR PHARMACIST
boxes.text1: Several services* related to skin health are offered in pharmacy:
boxes.note: *These services are offered at participating pharmacies only.
list: Vaccination and treatment against shingles.
Medication prescription to treat cold sores, mouth ulcers and acne.

boxes.title: PREVENTION & TREATMENT OF SHINGLES
boxes.text1: If you’ve had chickenpox, you could be among the ones who contract shingles. Rapid treatment, especially within the first three days of getting shingles, can reduce the duration and severity of illness.
boxes.linkLabel: Learn to prevent and treat shingles

cards.title: What’s the difference between psoriasis and eczema?
cards.text1: Learn about the differences between psoriasis and eczema so you understand these skin conditions better.

cards.title: How to get rid of acne?
cards.text1: Acne needs to be treated as soon as it appears. Understand the causes of acne and follow our tips and advice to better control your acne.

cards.title: Itchiness and irritation
cards.text1: There are a lot of products that can be used to relieve or prevent minor skin conditions like itchiness and irritation.

cards.title: Most Common Skin Rash Causes, Types, and Treatments
cards.text1: Find out what causes skin rashes, including eczema and psoriasis, and discover effective ways to soothe these rashes.

cards.title: PRESCRIPTION RIGHT AWAY!
cards.text1: Your pharmacist can prescribe medication on the spot for minor health conditions if your personal situation requires it.

cards.title: ADVICE ON OTC MEDICATION
cards.text1: If you don’t know which over-the-counter medication to choose to relieve your symptoms, don’t be shy to ask your pharmacist!

cards.title: VACCINATION
cards.text1: Did you know you can get vaccinated against Shingles? The virus that causes chickenpox stays in your body and can reactivate at any time during your life.

smoking_cessation.introPara1: Even with all the information out there about the harmful impact of smoking, it can be hard to take action and quit. Find out how your pharmacist can help and get tips on how to achieve your goals.

boxes.title: SERVICES FROM YOUR PHARMACIST
boxes.text1: Several services* related to smoking cessation are offered in pharmacy:
boxes.note: *These services are offered at participating pharmacies only.
list: Prescription of medication to help quit smoking.
Advice on over-the-counter medications related to smoking cessation.

boxes.title: THE DIFFERENT TREATMENT OPTIONS AVAILABLE TO YOU
boxes.text1: There are some therapies, both medicinal and non-medicinal, that can greatly contribute to your success. They will help you feel good physically, while you work on other aspects, such as your smoking habits.

cards.title: Nicotine withdrawal symptoms
cards.text1: Learn more about the common nicotine withdrawal symptoms you can face when you stop smoking.

cards.title: Vaping vs. smoking: what are the differences?
cards.text1: Ever considered quitting smoking by buying an e-cigarette? Learn about the differences between the two and how to manage nicotine addiction.

cards.title: COPD and Quitting Smoking
cards.text1: If you have COPD and want to quit smoking, your pharmacist can help you. Find out how along with a few tips.

cards.title: Quitting Smoking & Heart Health
cards.text1: It is a proven fact that quitting smoking is good for your heart. Discover a few reasons why and strategies to butt out for good.

cards.title: ADVICE ON OTC MEDICATION
cards.text1: If you don’t know which over-the-counter medication to choose to relieve your symptoms, don’t be shy to ask your pharmacist!

cards.title: RESPIRATORY HEALTH
cards.text1: If you have asthma or are experiencing strep throat symptoms, talk to your pharmacist about tests to ensure your respiratory health is in order.

cards.title: SMOKING CESSATION
cards.text1: Your pharmacist can develop an action plan with you, suggesting the treatment that best suits your health and needs, while helping you through your withdrawal symptoms.

vitamins_natural_products.introPara1: No matter your age, your body needs vitamins and minerals to ensure all your vital functions. You will most likely meet your daily requirements by eating a healthy diet, but sometimes, a little boost doesn’t hurt - and your pharmacist can guide you in choosing the right product for you.

boxes.title: PHARMACIST TIPS
boxes.text1: Talk to your pharmacist if you consider taking vitamins and natural products. He or she will give you advice related to many health conditions:
list: Pregnancy and menopause
Prevention of osteoporosis
Improvement of digestive health
Improvement of sleep quality
Moderation of potential interactions between medications, vitamins and natural products.

boxes.title: CAN MELATONIN IMPROVE SLEEP?
boxes.text1: Discover if it is safe to take melatonin to improve sleep, what are its benefits and how to improve bedtime routine.

cards.title: Myths and Facts about Vitamins and Minerals
cards.text1: Debunk common myths about vitamins and minerals. Read on to find out whether adding supplements to your diet is a good choice and has positive effects.

cards.title: Avoid a lack of vitamin D
cards.text1: Discover why experts recommend that most Canadian adults take a daily vitamin D supplement for osteoporosis prevention and bone health.

cards.title: The Right Multivitamin for You
cards.text1: If you’re baffled by the array of supplements available at your pharmacy, read on to discover how to choose the right multivitamin for you and your needs.

cards.title: Vitamin or mineral deficiencies?
cards.text1: Discover the main vitamin and mineral deficiencies caused by very poor diets or medical problems, and how vegans, vegetarians, seniors and women can be particularly at risk.

cards.title: Weight Management
cards.text1: If you’re thinking about losing weight, your pharmacist can shed a light on helpful natural health products and make sure your medication doesn’t make you gain weight as a side effect.

cards.title: Customization
cards.text1: If you are allergic to certain components of your medication or don't like the taste, your pharmacist can find allergy-free formulations as a substitution or add flavour to improve its taste.

cards.title: Medication Review
cards.text1: Sit down with your pharmacist for a medication review to determine if any harmful effects or interactions are caused by combining your medication together, if one of your medication can be removed from your therapy and if there is cheaper medication available.
